projects.name: Apex FSD - StormHacks 2026 (Winner)
projects.description: Won Best Python Hack at Western Canada's largest hackathon with a self-driving AI that plays Forza Horizon by physically turning a real steering wheel through a 100 Hz PySDL2 control loop, and hands control back the instant a human grabs it. A PilotNet-style PyTorch CNN steers from screen pixels plus live telemetry, trained with DAgger so every manual correction becomes new training data. Saliency maps caught it fixating on roadside signs, so we cut the crash footage that taught it.

projects.name: Scheming - HackMIT 2026
projects.description: Built a lie detector for AI models that flags when a model's words contradict its own private reasoning, citing the exact line as evidence. Tested on AI agents playing Werewolf, it matched human judgment on 94% of 300 hand-labeled turns. Run on 1,500 real coding-agent sessions, it caught agents claiming things like "all tests pass" that their own logs contradicted, at 92% precision.

projects.name: YouTube Shorts AI Optimizer
projects.description: An AI agent that reviews draft YouTube Shorts before publishing and predicts where viewers will swipe away. Built on my own channel, which grew from 1.2K to 38K subscribers and 45M views, and now used by 100+ other creators. Its Gemini retention predictions hit 0.45 Spearman on 85 held-out Shorts, beating a veteran creator's 0.25. It ships as a remote MCP server on Cloud Run, where Cloud Tasks retries on idempotent workers completed 99.9% of reviews at launch, OpenTelemetry tracing and parallel tool calls cut p95 latency from 95s to 18s, and isolating comment text behind read-only tools blocked 98.5% of 200 prompt-injection attacks.

projects.name: GitIntent - UC Berkeley AI LLM Hackathon 2026
projects.description: A shared memory layer for AI coding agents that records every change with the prompt behind it. Agents recall failed attempts before repeating them, which helped them solve 8.3% more DeepSWE benchmark tasks than the same agent without memory across 36 runs. Every code change is indexed in Redis Stack with HNSW and BM25 under a SHA-256 hash, and the hybrid vector and keyword retrieval engine reaches ~93% recall@5.

projects.name: Inventory & Sales Automation Platform
projects.description: Custom infrastructure for my cross-platform resale business on Grailed, Depop, and eBay, which has tracked 60+ international orders and $6K+ in sales. A concurrent Go worker turns sale emails from Gmail and Pub/Sub into orders and skips duplicates by order ID, a Playwright service reposts listings weekly on a 30-day bump-then-reduce price cycle, and caching report queries in Redis, cleared on each new order, sped up the sales dashboard API 36×.

projects.name: Premier Predictor
projects.description: Scraped and cleaned English Premier League match data to train a model that predicts match outcomes. It uses a Random Forest classifier built with pandas and scikit-learn.

projects.name: Java OOP Quiz Application
projects.description: A Java study tool for CPSC 210 students, used by 5+ peers. It has a layered architecture with interface-based abstraction and JSON save/load. It has 100% JUnit test coverage.

projects.name: Vital-Sense Radar
projects.description: A non-contact monitor that estimates breathing and heart rate from Wi-Fi Channel State Information. Two ESP32-S3 boards send and receive the signal, and Python (NumPy, SciPy) processes it into vitals. No camera or wearable is needed.

projects.name: Chelsea FC Play Predictor
projects.description: A data pipeline that pulls Chelsea match data from FBref and Understat into PostgreSQL and computes features automatically. It feeds 7 statistical and ML models. An EV optimizer and a Streamlit dashboard sit on top.

projects.name: Photo Time Capsule
projects.description: A hackathon mobile app for making time-capsule photo albums. Users capture photos with the camera and discuss them in comment threads. Built with React Native, Firebase, and Expo Go.

projects.name: Minecraft Data Science Project
projects.description: Analyzed player engagement and subscription behavior on a Minecraft research server. It uses KNN classification with cross-validation to predict which players subscribe. Built in R with tidymodels.
